title: NYC Taxi Tip Amount Prediction: End to End Data ML Pipeline
text:
The NYC Taxi Tip Predictor is an end-to-end machine learning pipeline that predicts passenger tip amounts using historical NYC TLC data. Built to transition ride-share drivers from guesswork to a data-driven strategy, this system predicts high-yield zones and times to help drivers maximize their hourly earnings.


For ride-share and taxi drivers, the base fare covers the operational costs of the vehicle, but the tip amount dictates their actual profit. However, tipping behavior is highly volatile and unpredictable. Currently, drivers rely on intuition or simply chase high-volume areas, which often results in wasted fuel and time waiting for rides that yield poor tips.
This lack of actionable foresight creates specific pain points for two main groups: * For Drivers (Inefficiency): Drivers cannot easily identify which specific zones, times, or effective routes will yield the highest return on their time. They need data to know where to wait. * For Customers (Static Tipping): Customers are often prompted with rigid, static tip suggestions (e.g., 20%, 25%, 30%). Predicting an expected tip amount provides a dynamic, context-aware baseline that can help customers decide on a fair tip based on historical norms for that specific route and time.
The Solution:
This project introduces a predictive machine learning pipeline that shifts strategy from a reactive “guessing game” to a proactive, data-driven approach. By forecasting the exact tip amount based on spatial (pickup/drop-off zones) and temporal (time, day, rush hour) factors, this system empowers drivers to strategically position themselves in high-yield scenarios while offering transparent tip estimates for riders.

title: TalentFit Shortlister: AI-Powered Resume Screening System
text:
✨ Key Features

Bulk PDF Parsing: Seamlessly extract and clean textual content from multiple uploaded PDF resumes using pdfminer.
Dual-Engine Similarity Scoring:

TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency): Ensures essential industry keywords and hard skills from the JD are present in the resume.
BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers): Provides deep, semantic-level understanding of the resume’s context, evaluating the actual meaning behind a candidate’s experience.

Interactive HR Dashboard: A React.js frontend that visually presents ranked candidates alongside their match percentages, allowing HR personnel to select top choices via simple checkboxes.
Automated Email Outreach: Utilizes Regular Expressions (RegEx) to extract contact details from selected PDFs and automatically dispatches interview invitations via SMTP integration.


🧠 System Architecture & Workflow

Input: HR uploads a batch of candidate PDFs and pastes the target Job Description into the React interface.
Extraction: The backend parses the PDFs into raw text strings.
NLP Processing: Both TF-IDF and BERT models compute cosine similarity scores between each resume and the JD.
Ranking: Resumes are ordered by their similarity scores and returned to the frontend.
Automation: Upon HR selection, the backend extracts candidate emails and triggers SMTP notifications.

title: TalentFit Shortlister: AI-Powered Resume Screening System
text:
Project Overview
In today’s fast-paced recruitment environment, Human Resource (HR) professionals face the challenge of manually screening large volumes of resumes—a process that is both time-consuming and inefficient.
TalentFit Shortlister is an intelligent, automated resume shortlisting web application. By leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning-based similarity models, the system accurately matches bulk uploaded candidate resumes against a target Job Description (JD) without manual intervention. It closes the recruitment loop by automatically emailing the top-ranked candidates.

🎯 The Core Problem & Solution

The Problem: Traditional ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems) often rely on rigid keyword matching, rejecting highly qualified candidates, while manual screening suffers from human fatigue and bias.
The Solution: A dual-engine machine learning approach. By combining keyword analysis with deep semantic understanding, TalentFit Shortlister ensures that candidates who have the right skills—even if phrased differently—are accurately evaluated, ranked, and contacted.



✨ Key Features

Bulk PDF Parsing: Seamlessly extract and clean textual content from multiple uploaded PDF resumes using pdfminer.
Dual-Engine Similarity Scoring:

TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency): Ensures essential industry keywords and hard skills from the JD are present in the resume.
BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers): Provides deep, semantic-level understanding of the resume’s context, evaluating the actual meaning behind a candidate’s experience.

Interactive HR Dashboard: A React.js frontend that visually presents ranked candidates alongside their match percentages, allowing HR personnel to select top choices via simple checkboxes.
Automated Email Outreach: Utilizes Regular Expressions (RegEx) to extract contact details from selected PDFs and automatically dispatches interview invitations via SMTP integration.



🧠 System Architecture & Workflow

Input: HR uploads a batch of candidate PDFs and pastes the target Job Description into the React interface.
Extraction: The backend parses the PDFs into raw text strings.
NLP Processing: Both TF-IDF and BERT models compute cosine similarity scores between each resume and the JD.
Ranking: Resumes are ordered by their similarity scores and returned to the frontend.
Automation: Upon HR selection, the backend extracts candidate emails and triggers SMTP notifications.

title: NYC Taxi Tip Amount Prediction: End to End Data ML Pipeline
text:
🔄 Development Workflow
This project strictly adheres to a modular design pattern. To experiment with the pipeline or add new features, follow this standard sequence:

Update config.yaml (paths/directories) and params.yaml (model hyperparameters).
Define data structures in the entity module.
Update the ConfigurationManager within src/config.
Modify the relevant pipeline components (e.g., ingestion, transformation, training).
Integrate the updated components into the specific pipeline script.
Register the pipeline in main.py and update dvc.yaml to track the new execution graph.
Serve the updated model via the app.py Flask interface.

title: NYC Taxi Tip Amount Prediction: End to End Data ML Pipeline
text:
🏗️ System Architecture
This project is built using a modular, component-based architecture orchestrated by DVC (Data Version Control).

Data Ingestion: Automatically fetches and extracts the NYC Taxi dataset.
Data Validation: Enforces schema rules and generates a validation status. Acts as a “Circuit Breaker” to halt the pipeline if anomalous data is detected.
Data Transformation: Handles complex feature engineering:

Datetime extraction (weekend flags, AM/PM, trip duration).
Cyclical encoding for pickup hours using sine/cosine transformations.
Spatial feature engineering (airport zone mapping).
Target Encoding and Standard Scaling (saved as preprocessor.pkl to prevent data leakage during inference).

Model Training: Trains an SGD Regressor, logging hyperparameters (alpha, penalty) to MLflow via DagsHub.
Model Evaluation: Calculates regression metrics (RMSE, MAE, R2) and saves them to evaluation.json.
Inference Pipeline: A dedicated prediction engine wrapped in a Flask web application for real-time user predictions.

title: E-Commerce Customer Segmentation & RFM Engine
text:
💡 The Vision: Why this exists
Retailers bleed money by treating all customers equally. Sending a 20% discount to a VIP who was going to buy anyway destroys profit margins, while ignoring a fading loyalist guarantees silent churn.
This project is an intelligent end-to-end segmentation engine. It analyzes historical e-commerce buying habits using Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) metrics, automatically groups customers via Machine Learning algorithms (K-Means/Random Forest), and feeds those actionable personas into an enterprise reporting layer.
This dashboard goes beyond data visualization to act as a strategic decision-making engine. By executing the phased marketing recommendations generated by the model, businesses can achieve a projected 10.01% uplift in revenue.

title: E-Commerce Customer Segmentation & RFM Engine
text:
🔬 The Technical Edge: “Cluster-Then-Predict” Architecture
Most standard portfolios deploy brittle, distance-based unsupervised models (like K-Means) directly to production. Those are computationally heavy and easily broken by high-value extreme outliers.
This project utilizes a highly scalable, two-stage MLOps architecture:

Offline Discovery (Unsupervised + Heuristics): Historical RFM data was log-transformed, standard-scaled, and clustered using K-Means. Mathematical centroids were then combined with strict, visually verified business-logic rules to safely isolate outliers and generate highly accurate ground-truth labels.
Production Inference (Supervised RF): A Random Forest Classifier (RFC) was trained to learn these complex, non-linear segment boundaries.
The Deployment Advantage: Because tree-based models are natively immune to outliers, the live Streamlit dashboard bypasses clunky feature scaling entirely. It processes raw user inputs instantly to deliver lightning-fast, real-time segment predictions.


🏗️ End-to-End System Architecture


1. The Machine Learning Backend (Python)

ETL Pipeline: Extracted and cleaned the UCI Online Retail dataset (Dec 2009–Dec 2010), handling missing values and scaling variables.
Clustering: Deployed K-Means clustering to logically separate the customer base, mapping output labels to actionable business personas (e.g., Champions, At-Risk, Whales).



2. The Interactive Web App (Streamlit)

Built a dynamic front-end using Streamlit to allow data scientists and product managers to test the underlying RFM logic, view segment distributions, and interact with the Python prediction models in real-time.

[Raw Transactions] ➔ [RFM Feature Engineering] ➔ [K-Means + Visual Heuristics] ➔ [Labeled Dataset]
                                                                                        ↓
                     [Model Artifact: rfc.joblib] ⟵ [Random Forest Classifier] ⟵ [Labeled Training]
                                  ↓
[Streamlit UI] ➔ [Live Raw RFM Input] ➔ [RFC Inference Engine] ➔ [Targeted Marketing Strategy]


3. The Enterprise Reporting Layer (Power BI)

Data Modeling: Constructed a Star Schema connecting a central Fact_Transactions table with Dim_Customers and Dim_Calendar to mirror corporate Data Warehousing standards.
Executive Dashboard: Built a dynamic, 3-page Power BI report (.pbix file included in this repository) featuring AI decomposition trees and an exportable CRM targeting ledger for the marketing team to execute the Phase 1 and 2 email campaigns.

title: E-Commerce Customer Segmentation & RFM Engine
text:
🖥️ Dashboard Features

📊 Analytics: Track overarching business KPIs (Total Revenue, Unique Customers, Average Basket Value).
🤖 RFM Clustering: Analyze offline cluster centroids and 3D behavioral distribution maps.
🔍 Robust Inference Engine: This Segmentation Dashboard can identify hidden customer behavior & also can deal with outlier customers
Low Latency: The architecture is fast because it makes an intentional trade-off by heavy math happens offline, simple math happens online.

Technical Philosophy & Principles







Production-First Mindset


A high-accuracy model is useless if it cannot be served reliably. I prioritize containerization with Docker, deterministic environments, and lightweight API endpoints.









Business Value Over Complexity


The best algorithm is the one that solves the business bottleneck with the lowest maintenance burden. Simple, interpretable baselines always come first.









Reproducible Workflows


Data science requires strict version control. From data versioning with DVC to experiment tracking via MLflow, every step must be auditable and reproducible.
